pack.title: Parking & driveways
pack.description: Your spot, their car. Calm words before tow trucks.

scenarios.setting: Your driveway, blocked. The neighbor leans out their door.
scenarios.jab: I'll only be like ten minutes. Chill.

replies.line: I need out now. Move it, please.
replies.why: Now plus please is polite and non-negotiable at the same time.
Four syllables with no argument attached — there's nothing to debate.

replies.line: I believe you — and I still need out. Quick move?
replies.why: Believing them while holding your need keeps it neighborly and effective.

replies.line: Ten minutes? My driveway charges hourly.
replies.why: Invoicing the spot makes moving it the cheaper joke.
It states the property line as fact, which no charm can move.

trap.line: Park there again and I'm having you towed.
trap.why: Threatening the tow before asking the move makes you the street's problem.

scenarios.setting: Apartment lot. A stranger is in your assigned spot, windows down.
scenarios.jab: There's like twenty open spots. What's the big deal?

replies.line: The big deal is it's mine. One of those twenty is yours.
replies.why: It answers the question literally and points at the easy fix.
Ownership plus direction, no debate offered or accepted.

replies.line: Totally get it — but I pay for that one. Mind hopping over?
replies.why: Naming the lease turns it from preference into paperwork, politely.

replies.line: I named that spot. We're close. Pick another friend.
replies.why: Fake attachment to asphalt makes moving feel like a favor, not a loss.
It grants their premise and spends it against them in five words.
